text:
Adam Gaudette finally got on the board Saturday, and he did it twice in a sense. His power-play goal cut into Utah's lead in a game San Jose went on to win, and Markerzone noted he "wastes no time answering after a hit on Macklin Celebrini." Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest summed it up: "PP2 again gets the job done. Adam Gaudette well deserved."

Last season the former Hobey Baker winner scored 17 goals in 66 games for the Sharks, and Evolving-Hockey had most of his value coming from even-strength offense. This season he has dressed for only seven games, at under 10 minutes a night, with one goal on six shots. Seven games is far too few to judge anything, and that includes the ugly five-on-five numbers: San Jose has taken just 24% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. What has carried him before is where he shoots from. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the better forwards last season at getting chances from the area right in front of the net. Our range for his full season sits at 7 to 16 goals.
headline: Adam Gaudette breaks through on the power play
